title: vidtoolz.resolveProductionReadSessionProfile.v1
description: Sealed manifest of an isolated Resolve session profile: the link between an ACCEPTED production-read grant and one concrete Resolve process. Produced only by tools/generate_session_profile.py from an ACCEPTED authority record, its LIVE policy and the exact worker bytes. The profile directory it seals registers EXACTLY ONE Project Library — the authorized local Disk library — and its EXACT tree is described here, so identity never depends on interrogating a pre-existing handle. `governed` is deterministic (same inputs -> same governed_sha256) and is what the worker enforces; `provenance` records the runtime facts of this particular sealing, including the profile root's physical identity. The worker refuses unless: the manifest digest matches its command-line pin, governed_sha256 matches the governed block, the authority/policy/worker/facade digests match the ones it verified itself, the profile root is still the same physical directory, the profile tree on disk is EXACTLY the sealed tree plus at most the bounded volatile allowlist, no symlink exists anywhere under the root, the registration file is still exactly registration_line, and the live Resolve process was started strictly after seal_epoch by the launcher whose runtime attestation it also verifies.

governed_sha256.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators) of `governed`

session_id.description: deterministic digest of the grant this profile serves

authority_sha256.description: sha256 of the ACCEPTED authority record BYTES

policy_sha256.description: sha256 of the compiled policy FILE bytes: exactly the digest the worker is pinned to with --production-policy-sha256

worker_sha256.description: sha256 of the exact worker file permitted to use this profile

registration_line.description: the single Linux .dblist Disk registration the profile contains: '<name>:<canonical_root>::::DISK'

profile_env.description: environment variable -> path RELATIVE to provenance.profile_root; the attested process must carry exactly these absolute values

script_server_port.description: local Resolve scripting endpoint; every listening owner must be the attested process or a descendant of it

resolve_binary.description: the pinned Resolve executable. realpath, size and sha256 are all enforced at attestation; the digest is recomputed whenever the inode identity, size, mtime or ctime changes.

project_open_law.const: read the project the human already opened; never LoadProject/OpenProject/SetCurrentProject/SetCurrentDatabase

tree.description: the EXACT sealed file set: relative path -> {sha256}. At every operation the worker enumerates the profile root and requires this set plus, at most, the bounded volatile allowlist — nothing else may exist.

dirs.description: the exact directory set under the profile root

volatile_patterns.description: bounded allowlist of runtime paths Resolve may create for itself. Never authority-bearing and never used for identity; a pattern may not cover the registration area.

constrained.description: sealed paths Resolve may legitimately rewrite. Their content is not free: `config/.activedb` must still select only the one authorized local Disk library and may carry no network entry.

host_primitive.description: the APPROVED dedicated-capsule host boundary, verbatim. Independent host review approved it on 2026-09-22 (review manifest 84f5bcbc…, 31/31 verified). It is not descriptive: the worker re-derives every field from the running system before a production read is served, and again at every operation.

capsule_account.description: the dedicated account the worker and Resolve run as; the operator cannot enter it

broker_path.description: the root-owned zero-argument broker that drops into the capsule

runtime_root.description: the FROZEN ROOT-OWNED Resolve runtime. Never /opt/resolve: the operator can rewrite that one.

script_lib_relpath.description: the scripting extension, relative to runtime_root; production loads THIS file directly and never runs the vendor loader, whose fallback order ends in /opt/resolve

caller_identity.description: the account Hermes signs from, and the identity of the shared HMAC key. The key is owned by the operator and readable — never writable — by the capsule, so a compromised capsule cannot mint its own caller.

hmac_key_id.description: first 16 hex of sha256(key bytes); the worker recomputes it from the bytes it loaded

evidence_mask.description: absolute worker-evidence paths the capsule init covers with an empty read-only tmpfs in Resolve's own mount namespace: the journal, the replay guard, the evidence spool and the shared key. None of them may cover the authorized library, the frozen runtime or the sealed profile.

confinement.description: the confinement the capsule init installs on the Resolve child before exec. The seccomp filter is what makes the evidence mask durable: without it a capsule-root process could simply unmount the mask or bind the real directory back in.

profile_root.description: absolute, canonical (non-symlinked) local directory the session must be launched with; ephemeral, never inside the operator's own Resolve configuration, and never the physical parent of this manifest

seal_epoch.description: wall-clock seconds at sealing (recorded for humans and for the attestation ordering check; the authority-bearing comparison uses seal_uptime)

source_config.description: operator configuration directory the settings files were COPIED FROM; it is opened read-only and never modified, and its library list is never copied

profile_root_dev.description: st_dev of the profile root at sealing; rechecked every operation

profile_root_ino.description: st_ino of the profile root at sealing; rechecked every operation

seal_uptime.description: seconds since boot at the moment of sealing, from /proc/uptime. The worker requires the Resolve process's own boot-relative start (stat field 22 / SC_CLK_TCK) to be STRICTLY greater than this: both come from the same monotonic clock, so a seal and a launch inside the same wall-clock second are still ordered exactly.

seal_boot_time.description: /proc/stat btime at sealing; a reboot makes the profile stale and every read refuses
